newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany fails to make competitiveness strides - poll.
newsitem.headline: Germany fails to make competitiveness strides - poll.

text.p: Germany is failing to make itself more competitive and is losing market share to leaner, meaner foreign competitors, a survey of leading German economic groups conducted by Die Welt newspaper showed on Monday.
According to the survey, several of the associations put the blame for Germany's lack of competitiveness on high labour costs and taxes.
The BGA Federation of German Wholesale and Export Trade said, for example, "We have enough work in Germany, but it is too expensive."
The BDI Federation of German Industry, meanwhile, said high social payments tied to wages further hurt German industry.

The DIHT German Federation of Chambers of Commerce told Die Welt that German industry was not becoming less competitive, only that other nations such as the U.S. and Japan were becoming more competitive.
The institute called for reform of corporate taxes and the elimination of the trading capital tax. It also called for reduction of red tape in environmental regulations.
